title: Introduction to Chemistry - Chemistry - Scientific Method
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the scientific method, a **hypothesis** is best described as __________.
options: a concise statement summarizing the results of many observations
a tentative, testable explanation for a set of observations
a widely accepted explanation supported by a vast body of evidence
a rigid rule that nature never violates
questions.explain: A hypothesis is a tentative explanation that acts as a starting point for further investigation and experimentation.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: The statement "Matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction" describes what happens in nature without explaining *why*. This is an example of a __________.
questions.explain: A Scientific Law summarizes a vast number of experimental observations and describes or predicts some facet of the natural world (often mathematically) but does not explain the underlying cause.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following statements distinguishes a **theory** from a **law**?
options: A law explains *why* nature behaves a certain way; a theory summarizes *what* happens.
A theory is a guess; a law is a proven fact.
A theory explains *why* nature behaves a certain way; a law summarizes *what* happens.
Laws can be proven false, but theories cannot.
questions.explain: Theories are comprehensive, testable explanations of particular aspects of nature (the 'why'). Laws describe observations (the 'what'), often mathematically, without necessarily explaining the mechanism.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which step typically follows the formulation of a hypothesis in the scientific method?
options: Conducting experiments to test the hypothesis
Changing the data to fit the hypothesis
questions.explain: Once a hypothesis is proposed, the next step is to design and perform experiments to test its validity.
questions.subject: Chemistry
